title: Rosalind and the Tide
premise: Ulyana Montrose has spent nine years keeping her heart in the past tense, running Saltwick's only bookshop and raising her daughter alone after the father vanished. When a freak snowstorm traps her overnight in the shop with Elias Thorne—the rival bookseller who broke her heart in their twenties and has just returned to buy the building housing her beloved bakery—old wounds and older sparks reignite. As the bakery lease deadline looms, Ulyana must choose between the safety of invisibility and the terrifying wholeness of loving again, discovering that the found family around her was always the home she refused to claim. She ends the story by signing the lease herself, buying the bakery, and choosing Elias not as a rescue but as an equal.
about_author: Cyrus Almeida is the pen name of a former coastal bookseller who now writes love stories from a drafty cottage in the north. They believe the best romances begin where duty ends.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine morning in Saltwick's bookshop: opening the shutters, school-run chaos, her daughter Wren's questions about the bakery's 'closed' sign. Establishes her careful, controlled life and the lease notice she's been avoiding. Beat: quiet dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Hands
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Elias Thorne walks into the bookshop after nine years away, asking about the Harrow Street property—the building that holds her bakery and her landlord's patience. She serves him with glacial politeness while her hands shake. Beat: the past arrives wearing a good coat.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ulyana's POV. Their twenties: the summer romance, the scholarship he took to Edinburgh, the promise he broke by leaving without goodbye while she was pregnant. Beat: explaining exactly why she keeps love in the past tense.

chapters.title: The Bakery That Raised a Child
chapters.summary: Wren's godmother Priya's POV. Priya runs the bakery under threat of lease termination; Ulyana quietly covers her shortfalls. Introduces the town's found-family web and the landlord's son circling the property. Beat: love expressed as labor, never words.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He's not the buyer—he's the surveyor hired by a faceless development firm, and he hasn't told anyone. He walks Saltwick mapping what his report will destroy. Beat: guilt arriving ahead of schedule.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Wren, eight and sharp, asks why the bakery man looks at Mama 'like a story she stopped reading.' Ulyana deflects, then finds Elias's old bookmark in a returned book. Beat: the past refuses to stay shelved.

chapters.title: An Offer, Poorly Worded
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He offers Ulyana a private heads-up about the development in exchange for her silence, hoping to buy time. She reads it as him buying her off and throws him out. Beat: two people protecting themselves into misunderstanding.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The forecast turns ugly; the town battens down. Priya, sensing history, schemes to leave Ulyana and Elias locked in inventory together at the shop's late stocktake. Beat: found family as gentle conspiracy.

chapters.title: Snowfall at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The storm hits early. Roads close, Priya's car won't start, and Elias, stranded after checking the property, takes shelter in the bookshop. Wren is safely with a neighbor. Beat: the world shrinks to two people and ten thousand books.

chapters.title: Candlelight Inventory
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Power fails; they work by candlelight, cataloging stock. Old rhythms resurface—she still knows his shorthand, he still finishes her sentences. First real conversation in nine years. Beat: muscle memory of intimacy.

chapters.title: Nine Years in One Night
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He confesses why he really left: his family's collapse, a debt he thought he was sparing her from, and the cowardice of the unsigned letter he still carries. She doesn't forgive him. Beat: truth without absolution.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Alone in the storeroom, she finds the unsent letter tucked in a returned book years ago and never opened. She reads it now, hands shaking. Beat: grief re-opened, but also re-understood.

chapters.title: Morning After the Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Snowbound roads open; Elias leaves before she wakes, leaving coffee and an apology in pencil. The town wakes to a transformed landscape and gossip. Beat: the tenderness of unfinished sentences.

chapters.title: The Landlord's Son Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Callum Renner offers Priya a new lease at triple rent unless the development deal falls through. The found family realizes the bakery has weeks, not months. Beat: the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Convenience
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Elias proposes they work together to kill the development—his insider access, her community leverage. She agrees, strictly professionally, and both know it's a lie. Beat: love sneaking in under a business arrangement.

chapters.title: Reading the Fine Print
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In the development documents he finds a clause: the project dies if the building gains heritage status or a sitting tenant-purchase. Hope, and a dangerous idea. Beat: the plot's engine turns over.

chapters.title: Wren and the Cartographer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (limited third). Wren interrogates Elias over hot chocolate, extracting a promise to draw her a map of Edinburgh. Elias realizes he's falling for both of them. Beat: the child as truth-teller.

chapters.title: Petition Night at the Anchor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The town pub hosts a petition drive for heritage status. Rivalries and old grievances surface; Ulyana speaks publicly for the first time in years. Beat: a woman finding her voice in public before she finds it in private.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. After the meeting, a near-kiss in the snow outside the Anchor, interrupted by Callum Renner's arrival and a barbed remark about Elias being 'the firm's man.' Elias doesn't deny it fast enough. Beat: the almost that hurts worse than a no.

chapters.title: The Report on His Desk
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His employer demands the final survey by month's end. He sits with two versions of the report on his desk and cannot type either. Beat: duty and desire in open conflict.

chapters.title: What Priya Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Ulyana: 'You're lending him pieces of yourself again, and calling it prudence.' A fierce, loving argument about self-protection versus risk. Beat: the theme spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Heritage Hearing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The council hearing on heritage status. Elias testifies—revealing his employment and the firm's plans, torching his career to save the building. Beat: public sacrifice, private fallout.

chapters.title: Betrayal or Salvation?
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The town is grateful; Ulyana is furious that he risked everything without telling her, repeating the pattern of unilateral decisions. They fight properly for the first time. Beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Firm Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Fired and blacklisted, Elias receives a final offer: reinstate and complete the survey, or face a lawsuit over the leaked documents. Beat: the antagonist tightens the screw.

chapters.title: Wren's Map Arrives
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Elias, keeping his promise, sends Wren a hand-drawn map of Edinburgh with a note: 'This is where I got lost. I'm trying to find my way back.' Wren shows Ulyana. Beat: the child as bridge.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Elias withdraws to protect her from the lawsuit, going silent. The bookshop feels emptier than before he came. Ulyana catches herself setting out two coffees. Beat: the cost of invisibility, finally felt.

chapters.title: Callum's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Callum, rattled by the hearing, offers Ulyana personally a deal: her silence and support for the development in exchange for a guaranteed lease for the bakery. Beat: temptation wearing a helpful face.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana takes stock—literally—of everything Elias has done, everything she's withheld, and the letter she never answered. She writes her reply. Beat: the decision crystallizing on the page.

chapters.title: What Wren Wants for Her Birthday
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Asked what she wants for her birthday, Wren says only: 'For Mama to stop being sad in the good way and start being scared in the good way.' Beat: devastating clarity from a child.

chapters.title: The Lawsuit Letter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Served with papers, Elias drafts a confession to shield Ulyana and prepares to leave Saltwick for good. He leaves the unsent confession with Priya, 'in case I lose my nerve.' Beat: the lowest point.

chapters.title: Priya Intervenes
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya reads the confession and refuses to be a post office for cowardice. She marches to the bookshop and forces Ulyana to read it. Beat: found family refusing to let love fail quietly.

chapters.title: The Chase Through Snow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana runs through the slush to the harbor guesthouse, but Elias has already left for the ferry. She stands on the dock as the boat pulls out—and turns to find him walking back up the road, having jumped off. Beat: climax of reunion.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the frozen harbor road, the full confrontation: his cowardice, her invisibility, the letter, the years. They choose each other out loud, without conditions. First kiss in nine years. Beat: the emotional climax.

chapters.title: Facing the Firm
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Together they meet the development firm's lawyer; Ulyana reveals she has spent the week gathering tenant-purchase commitments and heritage evidence. The firm, facing bad press, withdraws. Beat: plot climax—duty defeated by collective love.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana signs the tenant-purchase for the building—bakery, bookshop, and all—using the inheritance she'd been hoarding against disaster. Priya weeps into the flour. Beat: safety chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Letter, Answered
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She gives Elias her nine-years-late reply to his unsent letter. He reads it on the harbor wall. Neither speaks; nothing needs saying. Beat: the past tense finally closed.

chapters.title: Wren's Birthday
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A small party in the bakery: Priya's cake, the town's found family, and Elias formally, nervously, asking Wren's permission to stay. She grants it with an eight-year-old's magnanimity. Beat: joy, earned and uncomplicated.

chapters.title: Shelf by Shelf
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Quiet epilogue-in-motion: they reorganize the merged shop inventory, his shorthand and hers blending. Elias asks what she wants next; she answers without flinching. Beat: the new normal, tender and specific.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. One year later: the bakery thrives, the building is heritage-listed, Callum has left town. Priya watches Ulyana laugh across the shop and reflects on the family they built. Beat: gratitude, and the theme resolved.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Tide
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Wren asks why the shop's rare first edition is called 'Rosalind and the Tide.' Ulyana begins the story—their story—with 'Once, a woman kept her heart in the past tense.' Beat: love becoming the story they tell.
